text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Romanian refineries are expected to start operating normally in 10 days' time as smooth crude oil supplies are resumed.
- One more company - Uztel SA oilfield equipment maker -- joined in trading on the Bucharest stock exchange.
- A court in the Transylvanian city of Cluj is expected to rule on the fate of troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA -- liquidation or reorganisation -- in a week's time.
- There are not enough tractors in Romanian agriculture. The area assigned to one tractor is seven times larger than elsewhere in Eastern Europe.

- The Communications Ministry signed a contract on Wednesday with the Mobifon consortium, one of the successful bidders in the tender of a GSM licence in Romania, despite complaints by other bidders over the way in which the tender was organised.
- A plan for the financial recovery of Dacia Felix bank proved invalid, investors to help the beleaguered bank could not be found and the central bank considers the bank has no chance of survival.
- An adequate monetary policy will help the central bank to secure the stability of prices, said Thomas Davis, vice- president of the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, who visited Romania.
- The machine-building plant in the western town of Resita, famous for its products in the inter-war period, is expected to seek a stock exchange listing.
- An International Monetary Fund technical mission is expected to arrive in Romania next week for talks with the new government.
